To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
polymorphisms of the MTHFD1 gene and of the MTRR gene were associated with AAA susceptibility.

polymorphisms rs8003379 in MTHFD1 gene (odds ratio 0.41) and rs32611 8 in MTRR gene (odds ration 0.47) are associated with abdominal aortic aeurysm (AA) after adjusting for cardiovascular risk factors and chronic obstructive pulmonay disease (COPP).
the polymorphisms rs8003379 in MTHFD1 and rs326118 in MTRR genes resulted to be independent susceptibility factors for AAA.

the identification of genetic determinants of AAA and the elucidation of their biological function.
the identification and characterisation of genetic factors associated with AAA, with the aim to identify novel therapeutic and preventive strategies for the disease.
a better understanding of the role of polymorphisms in AAA susceptibility.

the genetic background for the development of AAA is very complex, and that a number of polymorphisms in the genes involved in methonine metabolism are involved in this process.

the genetic variability in methionine cycle may play an important role in the development of AAA.
